jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re searching for a collaborative, creative and data-focused Associate Manager , Product Marketing to partner with our Marketing and Guest Experience product teams to bring our latest technology innovations to market. As a Product Marketing Manager focusing on the SevenRooms venue management system and Front-of-House tooling, you will work cross-functionally as well as with external partners and customers to drive go-to-market activity – inserting the voice of the customer into every point of the product life cycle and communicating the rollout of new products both internally and externally. SevenRooms Marketing & Guest Experience products are on a remarkable trajectory and we’re looking for a driven Product Marketing Manager to help us create, evaluate, and increase adoption across the platform.

At SevenRooms, our Product Marketing  team is the driving force behind our brand's growth and visibility in the hospitality industry. Comprised of creative thinkers, data-driven strategists, and innovative storytellers, our marketing professionals are passionate about connecting with our audience and showcasing the transformative power of our platform. From crafting compelling campaigns and engaging content to nurturing leads and fostering customer relationships, our team works collaboratively to deliver impactful results and drive measurable business outcomes. With a focus on innovation, creativity, and customer-centricity, the Product Marketing at SevenRooms is dedicated to empowering hospitality professionals to thrive in an ever-evolving digital landscape.

This role reports to the Manager of Product Marketing.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Build business cases for new product/feature development in the Venue Management area of the product. Review and refine product requirements to fit customer & business needs. Leverage data and client product metrics to develop business cases around core products and features. Gather and distill market feedback and key industry learnings to help shape and prioritize the product roadmap.

- Develop and execute growth plans to drive wider client adoption of our Venue Management products.

- Manage beta testing to ensure successful launches and to accelerate product-market fit.

- Partner cross-functionally with Product, Enablement, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success to design and execute go-to-market strategies for our products.

- Partner with Brand, Growth and Customer Marketing on thoughtful, integrated marketing campaigns that drive usage and adoption across the platform.

- Work closely with the broader Product Marketing team to design & lead the GTM process – implementing standards from inception to launch. Drive internal communication cross-functionally ensuring the right stakeholders are involved and informed at the right time. Produce new and engaging product content and narratives as they relate to the SevenRooms products.

- Monitor competitive intel and market trends, developing strategies for knowledge sharing while incorporating these learnings into ongoing campaigns

- Collaborate closely with stakeholders throughout SevenRooms to obtain buy-in for product initiatives while setting clear expectations and goals.

We’re excited about you because you have…

- 3-6+ years of B2B product marketing experience

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- Experience working cross-functionally or with clients, including expectation setting, discovery and collaboration, and successful delivery of offerings

- Ability to quickly understand a specific client domain and identify the trends and opportunities in that space

- Curiosity to dig several layers deep into solutions with an eye toward continuous improvement and creative thinking

- Experience working in Hospitality and knowledge of restaurant and hotel operators preferred but not required

- Experience working with email and retention marketing products is a plus

- An open mind and flexibility around testing new approaches and the ability to harness failures and turn them into wins

About the Team

DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you want to work on commercializing autonomy and robotics in a service used by millions of people — and on bringing the merchant partners who power that service along with us — then we want to talk to you!

About the Role

Come help us redefine last-mile logistics through robotics, automation, and other advanced technologies. Autonomy only works when merchants — restaurants, retailers, and other partners — can reliably interact with our robots: handing off orders, troubleshooting edge cases, and trusting the experience enough to keep using it. This role owns that side of the equation.

We're looking for a Merchant Success & Growth lead to build the strategy and operational mechanisms that get merchants onboard, keep them performing, and turn their day-to-day reality into a tight feedback loop for product and engineering.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Own merchant adoption and performance KPIs for autonomy end-to-end — defining what "successful merchant interaction with a robot" means, instrumenting it, and driving improvement against it.

- Build the playbooks and operational mechanisms to onboard merchants to autonomy — from first conversation through training, go-live, and steady-state ops — and scale them across markets.

- Partner with sales, account management, and field ops to recruit and ramp the right merchant cohorts for each stage of the product, and design experiments that test new merchant-facing features and handoff models.

- Define merchant performance benchmarks (handoff success rate, dwell time, dasher/robot interaction quality, merchant CSAT) and run the cadence that holds partners and internal teams accountable to them.

- Stand up the feedback loop from the field back to product and engineering — turning merchant complaints, edge cases, and frontline observations into prioritized inputs that change what we build next.

- Be the voice of the merchant inside Labs: advocating for their constraints in product reviews, roadmap planning, and launch decisions.

We're excited about you because…

- You have a Bachelor's degree in business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent related experience.

- You have 3–6 years of experience in Strategy & Operations, Merchant/Partner Success, Product Operations, Business Strategy, or a closely related field — ideally with time spent owning a partner-facing KPI end-to-end.

- You've built operational mechanisms from scratch — onboarding flows, performance reviews, escalation paths, feedback loops — not just run mechanisms someone else designed.

- You're comfortable in the field. You'll spend time with merchants and on-the-ground ops teams, and you treat that as a feature, not a bug.

- You think in metrics. You can define a KPI, instrument it, and tell the difference between a real signal and noise.

- You communicate clearly across audiences — translating frontline merchant pain into crisp product asks, and translating product/engineering tradeoffs back into language merchants and field teams understand.

- You're biased toward action in ambiguous, early-stage environments. You're energized by problems that don't yet have an owner or a process.

About the Team

DoorDash’s centralized, global TPM organization helps Engineering deliver the company’s most complex and consequential technical, product, and business transformations. The team spans DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo and partners across a global Engineering organization of approximately 4,000 engineers.

We have intentionally built a lean, high-leverage TPM organization with a high bar for technical depth, business judgment, and independent domain ownership. Our leaders stay close to the business and technical work, lead through strong senior IC TPMs, and shape the operating mechanisms that allow complex organizations to execute at speed.

This Director will lead 12 TPMs (one-quarter of the global TPM organization) and report directly to the VP of Engineering Operations. Their team supports nearly 1,300 engineers across five strategically important organizations: Dasher & Logistics, Ads & Promotions, Merchant, DashOS, and Platform Services.

About the Role

As Director of Technical Program Management, you will lead a high-performing team of TPMs embedded across some of DoorDash’s most important and technically complex businesses. Your portfolio spans the real-time fulfillment network that powers every delivery, a multi-billion dollar ads revenue platform, DoorDash’s merchant ecosystem and in-store technology, and platforms that enable merchants and other businesses to access our logistics network through offerings such as Drive and Parcels.

You will partner closely with a VP and four Senior Directors to set direction, strengthen execution, develop TPM talent, and solve the cross-organizational challenges that sit between teams, systems, and business priorities. You will also play a central role in Pedregal, DoorDash’s multi-year global platform re-architecture across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo while maintaining production availability and continuing to build for each business’ evolving requirements.

We believe the future of TPM leadership is defined by leverage, not layers. This role is for a forward-looking leader who can develop an intentionally lean, high-performing team, use AI to amplify its impact, and shape strategy and organizational capability while remaining meaningfully connected to the work.

You must be located near San Francisco, CA, Sunnyvale, CA, or Seattle, WA for this hybrid position.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Lead and develop 12 TPMs supporting nearly 1,300 engineers across five strategic engineering organizations.

- Partner with senior Engineering and Product leaders to shape portfolio strategy, investment tradeoffs, technical sequencing, risk management, and organizational operating models.

- Help scale DoorDash’s core delivery network; accelerate the next several billion dollars of Ads growth; build the merchant operating system; and expand access to DoorDash logistics through Drive and Parcels.

- Establish durable mechanisms for execution, technical readiness, decision-making, and cross-functional alignment across highly interdependent organizations.

- Develop exceptional TPM talent and create an environment where senior ICs can own broad, strategic scope and serve as trusted partners to Engineering leadership.

- Help define the next evolution of a modern TPM organization, identifying the strategic initiatives, technical transformations, and organizational capabilities where AI-enabled ways of working can increase the pace and quality of execution.

- Deep commitment to developing talent and building culture within your team, setting a high bar for technical depth, ownership, sound judgment, and independent execution. You hire, coach, and promote strong TPMs who are technical leaders, focus on outcomes over process, and consistently deliver business value while improving engineering efficiency and collaboration.

- The technical and business judgment to identify and align your team to the highest-impact opportunities as well as make thoughtful investment and sequencing tradeoffs.

- The technical credibility to engage with Engineering leaders on architecture, platform migrations, system dependencies, reliability, and risk, while translating that complexity into clear decisions and execution plans.

- A track record of leading large-scale, multi-year transformations that require alignment across multiple organizations, systems, products, and stakeholders.

- An instinct for building durable operating mechanisms rather than relying on personal heroics: clear ownership, decision forums, execution cadences, risk management, and accountability.

jobs.title: Product Manager Airspace & Autonomy - DoorDash Air
jobs.description:
About the Team

The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale.

DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.

About the Role

As the Product Manager Airspace & Autonomy for DoorDash Air’s Airspace and Autonomy capabilities, you will own the end-to-end product strategy for the software, services, autonomy, perception, human interfaces and related capabilities required to deploy autonomous drone delivery at scale.

You will connect DoorDash’s order and logistics platform with the aircraft, autonomy stack, mission-planning services, UTM capabilities, fleet-management tools, and operator workflows that execute each delivery. You will define how an order moves from merchant readiness through dispatch, airspace validation, autonomous flight, delivery, and completion within the broader DoorDash marketplace, ensuring that new features align to DoorDash Air’s roadmap across teams while balancing execution timelines against technical debt.

You will lead product direction across autonomy, aviation software, services, hardware, systems engineering, flight operations, UTM, safety, regulatory, data, and DoorDash platform teams. You will work closely with the Head of UTM and senior Engineering and Operations leaders to establish the product roadmap, clarify system boundaries, make build-versus-partner decisions, and align technical investment with operational scale and unit economics. You will also coach and mentor engineers to help them understand how their work contributes to the broader vision and enables safe and scalable drone delivery operations.

This is not a coordination-only role, nor is it purely an internally facing role. You will already have deep credibility in standards development organizations and will promote best practices to help ensure that DoorDash Air’s software, services and hardware meet technical standards required for regulatory compliance in the U.S. and abroad. You will set the vision, establish priorities, make informed technical and product tradeoffs, and hold cross-functional teams accountable for delivering an integrated drone delivery system.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Own the end-to-end product strategy for DoorDash Air’s safety critical software, services and platform infrastructure. Define the long-term vision, platform architecture, capability roadmap, and investment priorities across aircraft, onboard software, cloud services, operational tooling, and DoorDash platform integrations.

- Integrate drone delivery into the DoorDash marketplace. Define how merchant preparation, order readiness, dispatch timing, routing, customer promises, delivery-zone eligibility, and fulfillment decisions interact with aircraft availability, weather, airspace, and operational constraints.

- Lead the autonomy product roadmap. Establish priorities across mission planning, autonomous path and motion planning, contingency behaviors, rerouting, detect-and-avoid integration, vehicle health, payload handling, landing and delivery behaviors, and remote assistance.

- Create the roadmap to progress from 1:1 to m:N operations. Define the incremental technical capabilities required to move from one operator supervising one aircraft toward increasingly autonomous multi-aircraft operations, including exception management, alert prioritization, task allocation, fleet orchestration, remote intervention, and human-autonomy interface design.

- Define the data strategy for autonomous aviation. Determine which geospatial, terrain, obstacle, weather, airspace, population-risk, connectivity, landing-zone, and operational data layers should be built internally, licensed, sourced through partners, or generated by the fleet.

- Build UTM and airspace-management capabilities. Lead product requirements for operational-volume generation, strategic and tactical deconfliction, dynamic rerouting, airspace authorization, constraint management, conformance monitoring, and interoperability with UTM service providers and public airspace systems.

- Lead standards compliance and engagement. Champion compliance with relevant standards — ASTM F3201 (software), F3548 and F3411 (UTM-specific functions) — across the airspace software roadmap and specs. Maintain an active leadership role in ASTM standards-development activities on behalf of DoorDash.

- Productize regulatory compliance. Translate Part 135 operating requirements, BVLOS approvals, safety cases, operational limitations, and emerging Part 108 concepts into reusable software, data, workflow, auditability, and configuration-management capabilities.

- Make build, buy, and partner decisions. Evaluate technology providers, data sources, autonomy components, and infrastructure partners based on strategic differentiation, integration complexity, operational risk, economics, and time to market.

- Define system-level success metrics. Work across the organization to establish instrumentation and KPIs across delivery success, order-to-dispatch time, route efficiency, intervention frequency, operator-to-aircraft ratio, aircraft utilization, mission completion, system availability, regulatory conformance, and cost per delivery.

- Connect technical investment to business outcomes. Develop business cases and sequencing recommendations that balance safety, customer experience, operational scalability, engineering effort, deployment speed, and long-term unit economics.

- Shape the technical organization. Identify the product, systems, autonomy, platform, data, hardware, test, and operational capabilities required to achieve the roadmap. Partner with functional leaders to define roles, close talent gaps, and build an organization capable of scaling beyond individual experts.

We’re excited about you because…

- 10+ years of product management, technical product leadership, systems leadership, or related experience, including significant responsibility for complex software or cyber-physical platforms.

- 5+ years of experience in autonomous systems, robotics, UAS, aviation technology, safety-critical systems, or another highly regulated real-world operating environment.

- A demonstrated track record of taking technically complex products from early concept or prototype through validation, deployment, and operational scale.

- Experience owning products that span multiple layers of a technology stack, including embedded or vehicle software, cloud services, APIs, data infrastructure, operational applications, and hardware integration.

- Strong technical fluency across autonomous-system concepts such as mission planning, path planning, motion planning, perception, localization, guidance and control, behavior management, contingency handling, simulation, telemetry, and command and control.

- Experience defining product strategy and architecture for distributed, real-time, or mission-critical systems in which reliability, safety, and operational performance are fundamental product requirements.

- Working knowledge of UTM, airspace-management systems, geospatial data, flight-planning services, operational volumes, conformance monitoring, and airspace interoperability.

- Experience operating within or building technology for FAA-regulated environments, including familiarity with any combination of National Airspace System hardware/software/procedures, Part 107, Part 135, Part 108, Part 146, BVLOS operating approvals, UTM or USS services, and evolving autonomous-flight regulations.

- Experience designing or scaling human-supervised autonomy, remote operations, multi-vehicle systems, fleet orchestration, or m:N operating models.

About the team

The People Product team builds the internal tools and frameworks that power every employee's journey across DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt. We combine a hybrid "build + buy" approach to deliver intelligent, scalable and people-centric experiences across hiring, compensation, onboarding, learning, performance and more — connecting our mission to empower local economies with the experience of the people who make it happen. We partner closely with Design, Engineering, Analytics, People/HR, Total Rewards and Talent Acquisition to build products that elevate the entire People Tech stack across all three brands.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the our internal compensation products — this includes the tooling, data, and AI that determine how DoorDash sets and maintains pay ranges across every job family, level, and country.

Range setting is the starting point, as it is the core process of a compensation team and the infrastructure everything else is built on. Your role is to turn that into a product: a range-setting workspace that ingests market and internal data to enable a Compensation Partner to review and make decisions.

This is an individual contributor role with a clearly scoped product area. The range-setting tool and the monitoring dashboard are the anchor. You will also own the seams into adjacent compensation surfaces — recruiter offer guidance, budget modeling, headcount planning, and Workday range loads — wherever they depend on range data.

What you'll be doing

- Own product decisions for the compensation range-setting stack — the range tool, its recommendation engine, and the monitoring dashboard — partnering with Compensation on methodology while owning how that methodology becomes product logic.

- Define the data pipelines and data products that range setting depends on — historical ranges, offers, incumbent, and attrition data — and own the partnership with People Analytics on the semantic layer and the proposed compensation data mart, including what the product requires of each.

- Own the range-setting product and analytics roadmap end to end and carry launches to market — adoption, enablement, and change management.

- Improve Compensation Partner productivity across the range review, while also managing intake, prioritization, and requirements definition for this part of the compensation stack.

- Own the seams into adjacent compensation products — recruiter offer guidance, budget modeling, headcount planning, and Workday range loads.

Requirements

- 5+ years of product management experience shipping products end to end, including at least one data- or workflow-heavy internal or B2B product.

- Demonstrated success turning a manual, judgment-heavy operational process into a product — rules, guardrails, recommendations, and measurable throughput gains — rather than digitizing a spreadsheet.

- Strong analytical skills and real comfort in data: you can size the problem, define the evaluation metric for a recommendation engine, read a precision-and-recall trade-off without flinching, and tell the difference between an anomaly and a statistically meaningful signal.

- Experience shipping an AI- or model-assisted feature where output quality is the product: rule or prompt design, evaluation sets, and honest measurement against human decisions.

- Excellent partnership and communication skills, including with the partners whose day-to-day judgment your product is encoding. You will need their trust to get their reasoning on the record.

- Experience working across custom-built tools and third-party SaaS (HRIS, ATS, survey and benchmarking, BI), including integrating data across systems and negotiating dependencies with platform and analytics teams.

Nice to have

- Direct experience with Compensation or Total Rewards — range architecture, market pricing, survey data, compa-ratio, peer groups, leveling, or annual budget planning.

- Familiarity with Workday, Greenhouse, Snowflake, and/or Sigma and their extensibility models.

- Experience building for multi-brand, multi-region, and multi-currency environments, and the data-privacy constraints that come with them.

- Experience shipping on top of a semantic layer, or enabling natural-language querying over a governed dataset.

About the Team

At DoorDash we’re building the industry’s most scalable and reliable delivery network to support our three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers. TPMs on our Engineering teams provide fundamental support to the underlying technology services as well as the engineers building these services. It’s no simple task, but it wouldn’t be interesting if it was!

About the Role

Platform Services is one of DoorDash’s organizations responsible for extending DoorDash beyond the consumer marketplace. The team owns three distinct business lines: Drive, a white-label delivery API that enables external businesses to access DoorDash’s delivery network; Parcels, which provides last-mile logistics for retailers and merchants; and Enterprise (DoorDash for Business), a b2b product suite powering corporate meal programs and large ordering for organizations of all sizes.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help scale Platform Services. You will lead important engineering wide initiatives across Enterprise, Drive, and Parcels, working with Engineering, Product, Operations, and business leaders to deliver dependable, extensible logistics capabilities for external businesses. Programs will span backend services, partner and merchant integrations, operational tooling, and platform interfaces. They require strong technical judgment, cross organizational coordination, stakeholder management, and ownership of results.

You will report into the centralized Technical Program Management team in Engineering.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Drive Platform Services’ Most Strategic Programs - You will partner closely with Engineering and Product leadership, Strategy & Operations, and cross-functional teams to turn Platform Services’ strategy into executable technical programs. The portfolio spans Drive (DoorDash’s white-label delivery offering), Parcels (last-mile logistics for merchants and retailers), and Enterprise (DoorDash for Business) a b2b corporate meal and large order fulfillment platform serving organizations of all sizes.

- Lead Complex Cross-Organization Execution - Platform Services depends on capabilities across logistics, merchant and partner integrations, dispatch and fulfillment, operational tooling, platform infrastructure, and the broader DoorDash ecosystem. You will establish clear ownership and milestones, surface critical dependencies and tradeoffs, and drive alignment across teams when the path forward is not obvious.

- Bring Technical Depth and Systems Thinking - You will develop a deep understanding of the architecture, integrations, data flows, and operational systems behind Drive,Parcels, and Enterprise. You will engage in technical designs, identify scaling and reliability risks, understand how decisions in one part of the system affect end-to-end delivery and partner experiences, and help teams make pragmatic tradeoffs.

- Turn Ambiguity into Strategy and Action - Many of our hardest problems do not begin with a clean scope or a single owner. You will truth-seek across technical and business inputs, frame the problem, clarify the definition of success, develop a point of view on risks and options, and create an execution path that teams and leaders can align behind.

- Connect Engineering Execution to Business Outcomes - You will understand the merchant, partner, customer, and economic outcomes behind the work and use that context to guide prioritization and execution. Whether the goal is expanding access to DoorDash logistics, improving delivery quality and reliability, enabling new partner use cases, or improving cost to serve, you will help teams stay focused on the technical work that matters most to the business.

- You’ve engaged with Engineering teams on product & platform development with a thorough understanding of software development processes and project planning.

- You are pragmatic and detailed in your approach and focus on progress, not perfection.

- Experience in large-scale distributed systems and system architecture.

- Experience working directly with engineering teams on product development, with a thorough understanding of software development processes, system architecture, and scalability trade-offs.
